T: Great Scott, that's a good burger.
D: A teenager accidentally travels back to 1955 and has to get his parents to fall in love.
P: Serve the mains when Marty walks into Lou's Cafe in 1955 and asks for a sugar-free drink.
S: Hand-cut chips blanched at 140C, fried at 185C until crisp, salted and served in a red-checked paper boat.

Soft pretzel bites dipped in a bicarb bath and baked deep brown, tossed in garlic butter and bright green parsley salt, with a cheddar dip. Mix 400g plain flour, 7g yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt and 250ml warm water, knead and prove 1 hour. Roll into ropes and cut into 3cm bites. Boil 2 litres water with 60g bicarb soda and dip the bites for 30 seconds. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Blitz a big handful of parsley with 1 tsp salt until bright green. Toss the bites in 40g melted butter with 1 crushed garlic clove, then the green salt.
Puff pastry brushed with egg, covered in cheddar, parmesan and cayenne, folded, cut into tall strips, twisted, baked at 220C for 12 minutes.
M: griddled onions, pickles and a slice of American
Thin onions pressed into a beef patty on a hot griddle, smashed, flipped, American cheese on top, pickles and mustard on a toasted bun.
eggs, bacon and toast, ideally not cooked by a robot arm

Thick bacon rendered crisp, basted fried eggs, grilled tomatoes, smoky baked beans and buttered toast, with dog food strictly not included. Fry 8 thick bacon rashers over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp and keep warm. Grill 4 halved tomatoes cut side down in the bacon fat for 4 minutes. Warm a 420g tin of baked beans with 1 tsp smoked paprika. Fry 8 eggs in the remaining fat, spooning hot fat over the whites until set. Toast and butter 4 thick slices of bread and serve everything on hot plates.
W: ocean blue frosting for the dance
Vanilla cupcakes baked at 180C for 18 minutes, piped with ocean blue buttercream, topped with sugar pearls and a gummy fish.
K: Vanilla ice cream blended thick with cold milk, chocolate syrup and malted milk powder, poured into tall glasses with whipped cream and two straws. Add 12 scoops vanilla ice cream, 800ml cold milk, 8 tbsp chocolate syrup and 8 tbsp malted milk powder to a blender, working in two batches if needed. Blend 30 seconds until thick but pourable. Pour into 4 tall chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of malted milk powder, and serve each with two straws.

dishes.make_ahead: Cut up to 4 hours ahead, keep in cold water then dry well

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into chips, rinse in cold water and dry thoroughly with a clean tea towel.
Heat the oil in a sturdy deep pan to 140C and blanch the chips in batches for 5 minutes without browning.
Drain and cool the chips for 15 minutes (this rest is part of the cook time).
Raise the oil to 185C and fry in batches until crisp, drain, season with salt and serve in paper boats.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, keep in an airtight tin

steps.text: Beat the egg and brush half of it over the pastry sheet.
Scatter over the cheddar, parmesan and cayenne, fold in half and press lightly.
Cut into 8 tall strips, twist each one and place on a lined tray. Brush with the remaining egg.
Bake at 220C conventional until puffed and golden.

dishes.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Divide the mince into four loose balls and slice the onion very thin.
Heat a griddle until very hot. Put the beef balls on it, top with onion and press firmly into thin patties. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook 3 minutes, flip and cook a further 2 to 3 minutes until the centre reaches 75C. Lay the cheese on top to melt.
Toast the buns and fill with the patties, pickles and mustard.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake up to 1 day ahead, ice on the day

steps.text: Beat about half the butter with the caster sugar until pale, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Fold in the flour and most of the milk. Divide among 8 cupcake cases.
Bake at 180C conventional until a skewer comes out clean, then cool completely.
Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar and a splash of milk until fluffy and tint blue.
Pipe onto the cakes and top with sugar pearls and gummy fish. Serve two small cupcakes each.

ingredients.item: malted milk powder, plus extra to sprinkle

steps.text: Blend the ice cream, milk, chocolate syrup and malted milk powder for 30 seconds, in two batches if needed, until thick but pourable.
Pour into tall chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of malted milk powder, and serve each with two straws.

edition.tagline: Great Scott, that's a good burger.
edition.cue: Serve the mains when Marty walks into Lou's Cafe in 1955 and asks for a sugar-free drink.

s.note: Hand cut chips, double fried until crisp and lightly salted.
s.how: Hand-cut 500g potatoes into chips, rinse and dry thoroughly. Heat vegetable oil in a sturdy deep pan to 140°C. Blanch the chips in batches for 5 minutes without browning, drain and cool 15 minutes. Increase the oil to 185°C and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp. Drain, season with 1/2 tsp fine salt and serve in red-checked food-safe paper boats.

s.note: Tall twisted pastry strips with cheddar, parmesan and a little cayenne.
s.how: Brush 1 sheet puff pastry with half of 1 beaten egg. Scatter over 60g grated cheddar, 20g grated parmesan and 1/8 tsp cayenne pepper. Fold in half and press lightly. Cut into 8 tall strips, twist each and place on a lined tray. Brush with the remaining egg. Bake at 220°C conventional for 12 minutes until puffed and golden.

m.note: Smashed onion beef patty with cheese, pickles and mustard.
m.how: Divide 600g beef mince into four loose balls. Slice 1 onion very thin. Heat a griddle until hot. Put the beef balls on the griddle, top with the onions and press firmly into thin patties. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Cook 3 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through, checking the centre reaches 75°C. Add 80g American-style cheese to melt. Toast 4 burger buns and fill with the patties, 60g sliced dill pickles and 30g yellow mustard.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes with ocean blue buttercream, sugar pearls and gummy fish.
w.how: Beat 80g softened butter with 80g caster sugar until pale. Beat in 1 egg and 1 tsp vanilla extract. Fold in 100g self-raising flour and 40ml milk. Divide among 8 cupcake cases and bake at 180°C conventional for 18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely. Beat 60g softened butter with 120g icing sugar and 1 tsp milk until fluffy. Tint with a little blue food colouring, pipe on the cakes and top with 10g sugar pearls and 8 fish-shaped gummy sweets. Serve two small cupcakes each.

d.note: Vanilla ice cream blended thick with cold milk, chocolate syrup and malted milk powder, poured into tall glasses with whipped cream and two straws.
d.how: Add 12 scoops vanilla ice cream, 800ml cold milk, 8 tbsp chocolate syrup and 8 tbsp malted milk powder to a blender, working in two batches if needed. Blend 30 seconds until thick but pourable. Pour into 4 tall chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of malted milk powder, and serve each with two straws.
